topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Following an APA contested-case hearing, which of the following sanctions may GREC impose on a broker under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(a)?
choice_a: Only permanent revocation, with no lesser sanctions available
choice_b: Refusal to grant or renew a license, reprimand, suspension, revocation, revocation with simultaneous reissuance as a salesperson license, cost-reimbursement assessments, or a fine
choice_c: Only a monetary fine, with no authority to suspend or revoke a license
choice_d: Only referral to the district attorney for criminal prosecution
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(a) gives GREC a full sanction menu: refusal to grant/renew, reprimand, suspension, revocation, revocation with simultaneous reissuance as a salesperson license, cost-reimbursement assessments, and a fine.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(a), what is the maximum fine GREC may impose per violation?
choice_d: There is no statutory cap on the fine amount
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(a) caps GREC's fine authority at $1,000 per violation.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), which of the following is an enumerated unfair trade practice ground for GREC discipline?
choice_a: Charging a commission rate above the local market average
choice_b: Declining to show a property that is currently under contract
choice_c: Requiring proof of pre-qualification before showing a listed property
choice_d: Discrimination in the sale or rental of property on protected-class grounds, discriminatory advertising, or blockbusting
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(1) enumerates fair housing violations -- discriminatory sale/rental conduct, discriminatory advertising, and blockbusting -- as an unfair trade practice ground for discipline.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(2), how does Georgia treat misleading or inaccurate real estate advertising by a licensee?
choice_a: It is an explicit, enumerated unfair trade practice subject to GREC discipline
choice_b: It is permitted as long as the listing broker's name appears somewhere in the ad
choice_c: It is regulated exclusively by the Federal Trade Commission, not GREC
choice_d: It is only a violation if the advertisement is in print, not online
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(2) enumerates misleading or inaccurate advertising as an unfair trade practice ground for GREC discipline.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), how is improper dual-capacity dealing by a licensee treated?
choice_a: As acceptable so long as the licensee personally profits from both sides
choice_b: As an enumerated unfair trade practice subject to GREC discipline
choice_c: As a matter left entirely to private civil litigation, outside GREC's authority
choice_d: As a violation only when the transaction involves commercial property
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(9) enumerates improper dual-capacity dealing as an unfair trade practice ground for GREC discipline.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), may a Georgia licensee guarantee a buyer future resale profits on a property as part of a sales pitch?
choice_a: Yes, as long as the guarantee is put in writing
choice_b: Yes, as long as the guarantee is limited to new construction
choice_c: No -- guaranteeing future resale profits is an enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_d: Yes, but only the qualifying broker personally may make such a guarantee
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(10) enumerates guaranteeing future resale profits as an unfair trade practice, regardless of whether it is written or limited to certain property types.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), within how many days after a listing expires must a licensee remove a 'for sale' sign from the property?
choice_c: There is no removal deadline once a sign has been properly placed
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(11) treats improper signage -- including failure to remove a 'for sale' sign within 10 days of listing expiration -- as an unfair trade practice.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), is it an unfair trade practice for a licensee to offer a property for sale or lease without the owner's knowledge and consent, or outside the terms the owner authorized?
choice_a: Yes -- this is an explicit, enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_b: No -- a licensee may market any property they believe is likely to sell
choice_c: No -- this is only a concern for exclusive listings, not open listings
choice_d: Yes, but only if the licensee also collects a deposit from a prospective buyer
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(12) enumerates offering property without the owner's knowledge/consent, or outside authorized terms, as an unfair trade practice.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), how does Georgia treat a licensee who induces a party to breach an existing brokerage agreement in order to substitute a new one?
choice_a: As a legitimate competitive practice so long as no written contract existed
choice_b: As an enumerated unfair trade practice subject to GREC discipline
choice_c: As acceptable if the new brokerage agreement offers a lower commission rate
choice_d: As a matter regulated only by the Georgia Association of Realtors, not GREC
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(13) enumerates inducing a breach of an existing contract or brokerage agreement to substitute another as an unfair trade practice.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), may a licensee negotiate directly with a party who has an exclusive listing or brokerage agreement with another firm?
choice_a: Yes -- exclusive listings do not restrict any other licensee's ability to negotiate with the party
choice_b: Yes, as long as the negotiation occurs after normal business hours
choice_c: No -- improperly negotiating directly with such a party is an enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_d: Yes, provided the licensee discloses the contact to GREC within 24 hours
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(14) enumerates improperly negotiating directly with a party who has an exclusive listing or agreement elsewhere as an unfair trade practice.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), may a real estate licensee who is not a licensed appraiser call a value opinion an 'appraisal'?
choice_a: Yes, as long as the licensee has at least five years of sales experience
choice_b: Yes, as long as the opinion is given orally rather than in writing
choice_c: Yes, provided the client is informed the licensee is not a certified appraiser
choice_d: No -- doing so without appraiser licensure is an enumerated unfair trade practice
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(15) enumerates calling an opinion an 'appraisal' without appraiser licensure as an unfair trade practice, regardless of experience, form, or disclosure.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b), how does Georgia treat a Georgia-licensed broker who practices real estate in another state without holding a license in that state?
choice_a: As an enumerated unfair trade practice subject to GREC discipline
choice_b: As outside GREC's jurisdiction entirely, since the conduct occurred outside Georgia
choice_c: As permissible reciprocity automatically extended to all Georgia licensees
choice_d: As a violation only if the other state files a formal complaint with GREC
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(16) enumerates practicing real estate in another state without that state's license as an unfair trade practice subject to GREC discipline.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: How does Georgia treat net listing agreements, under Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.06(1)(c)?
choice_a: They are permitted as long as the client signs a separate net-listing disclosure form
choice_b: They are categorically prohibited -- the Commission requires the broker's fee to be added, notifying the client of the gross price, rather than allowing the broker to keep everything above a net figure
choice_c: They are permitted only for commercial property
choice_d: They are discouraged but not prohibited, and remain enforceable if in writing
explanation: Rule 520-1-.06(1)(c) prohibits net brokerage engagements outright, obligating the broker to add the broker's fee and notify the client of the gross price -- net listings are categorically illegal in Georgia, not merely discouraged.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-31, what is the criminal classification of acting as a real estate licensee without a license, or otherwise violating O.C.G.A. Chapter 43-40?
choice_a: A misdemeanor only if the unlicensed conduct involves more than $50,000 in transaction value
choice_d: Chapter 43-40 violations carry no criminal penalty, only civil/administrative sanctions
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-31 makes unlicensed practice, or any other violation of Chapter 43-40, a misdemeanor, with no dollar-value threshold.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-27(a), to what time period is a GREC investigation of licensee conduct generally limited, and what are the exceptions?
choice_a: Generally limited to conduct occurring within 1 year, with no exceptions of any kind
choice_b: There is no time limitation of any kind on GREC investigations
choice_c: Generally limited to 3 years, but only for salesperson licensees, not brokers
choice_d: Generally limited to conduct occurring within 3 years of the investigation's initiation, with exceptions for fraud or fiduciary-fund-mishandling investigations and matters already in litigation
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-27(a) generally limits GREC investigations to conduct within 3 years of initiation, with exceptions for fraud/fiduciary-fund-mishandling cases and matters already in litigation -- and this applies to brokers as well as salespersons.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: How many hours of continuing education must a Georgia broker complete per 4-year renewal period, and how many of those hours must specifically cover license-law topics?
choice_a: 36 total hours, of which at least 3 hours must be on license-law topics
choice_b: 24 total hours, of which at least 6 hours must be on license-law topics
choice_c: 36 total hours, with no specific license-law-topic requirement
choice_d: 12 total hours, of which at least 3 hours must be on license-law topics
explanation: Georgia requires 36 instructional hours per 4-year renewal period, of which at least 3 hours must specifically cover license-law topics.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: What is the Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund, and how is it funded in Georgia?
choice_a: A fund financed entirely through annual state budget appropriations, with no connection to license fees
choice_b: A GREC-administered fund financed through a portion of the license activation fee -- $20 of the $45 individual activation fee and $20 of the $75 firm/school activation fee
choice_c: A privately administered fund unrelated to GREC, financed by voluntary broker donations
choice_d: A fund financed through the $1,000-per-violation fines GREC collects from disciplined licensees
explanation: The Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund is funded through a portion of the license activation fee: $20 of the $45 individual activation fee, and $20 of the $75 firm/school activation fee.
source_note: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.04(1) fee subsection
